stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: 2026 six-country sanctions wave
frames.note: The story begins with the coordinated 2026 sanctions packages from Norway, Canada, and partners targeting named settlers and outposts, alongside the London property-event flashpoint. Under this frame the record reads as a Western policy turn against specific networks, with prior decades as background. This is the frame Western foreign ministries and sanctions-tracking outlets open with.

frames.label: Oct 2023 post-attack surge
frames.note: The story begins with the sharp rise in settler attacks and Bedouin displacement after the Oct 2023 Gaza war started. Under this frame the record reads as a wartime acceleration of pre-existing settler activity, framing sanctions as a response to a recent spike. This is the frame UN OCHA reporting, EU diplomats, and many mainstream outlets open with.

frames.label: 1995 Oslo II Area A/B/C
frames.note: The story begins with the Oslo II accords carving the West Bank into Areas A, B, and C and the settler-outpost expansion that followed inside Area C. Under this frame the record reads as a long erosion of a signed framework, with the Jenin base plan and outpost legalization as the latest steps. This is the frame Palestinian negotiators, legal scholars, and Haaretz-style Israeli reporting open with.

frames.label: 1967 occupation begins
frames.note: The story begins with the 1967 war and the start of Israeli military rule over the West Bank, with civilian settlement following soon after. Under this frame the record reads as one continuous displacement process that sanctions only graze at the edges. This is the frame Palestinian civil society, Amnesty, and much of the Global South press open with.

bands.label: Six-country sanctions wave
bands.summary: Norway, Canada, the UK, and partners roll out fresh sanctions on settlers and outposts while a London property event and the Jenin base plan draw parliamentary and EU pushback.

nodes.title: Norway announces fresh sanctions on Israeli settlers
nodes.what: Norway's government rolls out a new round of sanctions targeting named Israeli settlers and entities tied to West Bank violence and outpost expansion. Palestinian officials and rights groups welcome the move; Oslo frames it as part of a coordinated European response to settler attacks on Palestinian civilians and herder communities in Area C.

nodes.title: UN reports record levels of West Bank settler violence in 2026
nodes.what: United Nations monitors release figures describing 2026 as the highest year on record for settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank, including assaults on villages, arson, and displacement of herder communities. The report feeds directly into the case Western governments are using to justify new sanctions packages.

nodes.title: Israel advances regulations to legalize West Bank farm outposts
nodes.what: Haaretz reports Israel is moving forward with new regulations designed to legalize so-called farm outposts in the West Bank, structures set up by settlers on grazing land outside authorized settlement boundaries. The package also includes a settlement funding plan sent to the security cabinet the same week.
nodes.disputed: The Israeli government describes the step as regularizing existing land use; Palestinian groups, EU diplomats, and Israeli NGOs describe it as legalizing seizures that drove Bedouin and herder families off the land.

nodes.title: Canada pledges 100 million dollars in aid citing settler violence
nodes.what: Ottawa announces 100 million Canadian dollars in new humanitarian funding for Palestinians, with officials explicitly naming settler violence and the humanitarian crisis in the West Bank and Gaza as drivers. The announcement comes alongside Canada's expanding sanctions list of individual settlers and outpost-linked entities.

nodes.title: London mayor and Amnesty target settlement property event
nodes.what: London mayor Sadiq Khan publicly condemns a planned event in the city promoting the sale of property in Israeli West Bank settlements, calling on the UK government to block it. The same day Amnesty International calls for a broad boycott of Israel over settler violence and conditions in the occupied West Bank.

nodes.title: UK MPs press to block event as EU's top diplomat raises alarm
nodes.what: A cross-party group of UK lawmakers urges the British government to block the London property event, citing legal exposure under UK sanctions on settlements and named settlers. The same day the EU's top diplomat publicly describes the surge in settler violence in the West Bank as alarming and places it at the center of the bloc's foreign policy agenda.

bands.label: First Western sanctions
bands.summary: The US, UK, EU, and Canada open targeted sanctions on individual settlers and outposts as settler violence and Bedouin displacement keep rising across Area C.

nodes.title: Biden signs Executive Order 14115 on West Bank settler sanctions
nodes.what: President Biden issued EO 14115, declaring a national emergency over settler violence in the West Bank and authorizing financial sanctions and visa restrictions against named individuals. The Treasury immediately designated four Israeli settlers under the order, freezing any US-linked assets and barring US persons from transacting with them. The order was the first dedicated US sanctions framework aimed at West Bank settler conduct.
nodes.disputed: The White House described the order as a narrow response to documented attacks on Palestinian civilians; Prime Minister Netanyahu's office described it as unnecessary, saying Israel handles lawbreakers through its own courts.

nodes.title: UK opens its own sanctions track on settlers
nodes.what: Foreign Secretary David Cameron announced UK sanctions on four Israeli settlers accused of human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank, imposing asset freezes and travel bans. The measure mirrored the US designations and made the UK the first European state to sanction settlers under its national regime. Cameron framed the move as a response to a sharp rise in extremist settler violence.

cites.l: BBC topic: Israel and the Palestinians

nodes.title: ICJ advisory opinion calls the occupation unlawful
nodes.what: The International Court of Justice issued an advisory opinion finding Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory unlawful and calling for it to end as rapidly as possible. The opinion addressed settlements, settler violence, and resource control among other issues. Though non-binding, the text became a reference point cited in later European parliamentary debates over settler sanctions.
nodes.disputed: The court majority described the settlement enterprise as a violation of international law that must be reversed; the Israeli foreign ministry described the opinion as fundamentally wrong and politically driven.

nodes.title: US Treasury expands sanctions to settler organizations
nodes.what: OFAC designated additional individuals and, for the first time, organizations linked to outpost activity and attacks on Palestinian villages. The action moved the EO 14115 regime beyond individual settlers and onto institutional actors operating in Area C. European foreign ministries welcomed the broadening, while the Israeli government formally protested it.

nodes.title: Trump revokes Executive Order 14115
nodes.what: On his first day back in office, President Trump rescinded EO 14115 alongside other Biden-era foreign policy orders, ending the US sanctions on the designated settlers and entities. The Treasury subsequently removed the relevant names from its sanctions list. The revocation left the UK, EU, and Canadian regimes as the main remaining Western settler-sanctions tracks.
nodes.disputed: The Trump White House described the revocation as removing a politically motivated tool aimed at an ally; rights groups and former US officials described it as removing accountability for documented violence.

nodes.title: Five countries sanction Smotrich and Ben-Gvir
nodes.what: The UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and Norway jointly announced sanctions on Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, citing incitement of settler violence against Palestinians. The measures included asset freezes and travel bans. It was the first coordinated Western sanctioning of serving Israeli cabinet ministers, and Israel summoned the five ambassadors in protest.

cites.l: BBC topic: Israel and the Palestinians

bands.label: Post-Oct 7 settler surge
bands.summary: After the Gaza war begins, UN and rights groups record a sharp rise in settler attacks, herder community displacement, and home demolitions across the West Bank.

nodes.title: Hamas attack on southern Israel triggers Gaza war
nodes.what: Hamas-led fighters crossed from Gaza into southern Israel, killing about 1,200 people and taking roughly 240 hostages. Israel declared war and began large-scale operations in Gaza, and West Bank movement restrictions and military raids intensified within days.

cites.l: UN OCHA - Hostilities in the Gaza Strip and Israel

nodes.title: UN OCHA records sharp rise in West Bank settler attacks
nodes.what: In the weeks after October 7, OCHA's protection updates documented a steep increase in settler violence incidents against Palestinians across the West Bank, including assaults, livestock theft, and property damage. OCHA also tracked a rise in Israeli military operations and Palestinian fatalities in the same period.

nodes.title: Bedouin and herder communities displaced from Area C
nodes.what: OCHA and rights groups reported that entire herder and Bedouin communities in Area C, including in the South Hebron Hills and Jordan Valley, were leaving their homes after repeated settler intimidation and access restrictions. Israeli officials described the moves as voluntary relocations while Palestinian residents and UN monitors described them as displacement under coercion.
nodes.disputed: OCHA and Palestinian residents describe the moves as forced displacement driven by settler violence and access restrictions; Israeli authorities describe them as voluntary departures from unauthorized encampments.

nodes.title: US executive order sanctions West Bank settlers
nodes.what: President Biden signed Executive Order 14115, authorizing financial sanctions and visa bans on individuals undermining peace, security, or stability in the West Bank. The Treasury Department's initial designations named four Israeli settlers accused of violent attacks against Palestinians.

cites.l: US Treasury - OFAC West Bank-related designations

nodes.title: UK and France announce sanctions on violent settlers
nodes.what: The British Foreign Office announced financial sanctions and travel bans against four Israeli settlers accused of human rights abuses against Palestinians in the West Bank, and France imposed parallel visa bans on dozens of settlers. The measures were framed as a response to a documented surge in settler attacks since October 2023.

cites.l: UK Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office
France Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs

nodes.title: ICJ advisory opinion on Israeli policies in occupied territory
nodes.what: The International Court of Justice issued an advisory opinion finding that Israel's continued presence in the occupied Palestinian territory was unlawful and that settlement activity violated international law. Israel rejected the opinion as politically motivated while Palestinian officials and many states cited it as legal grounding for further measures.

cites.l: International Court of Justice - case page
UN News - ICJ advisory opinion coverage

nodes.disputed: The Palestinian Authority and many UN member states describe the opinion as authoritative confirmation of illegality; Israel describes it as a one-sided advisory text that ignores security context and is not legally binding.

bands.label: Oslo II and outpost growth
bands.summary: Under the Area A/B/C split, authorized settlements expand and unauthorized outposts spread across Area C while successive Israeli governments regularize many of them.

nodes.title: Levy Committee report rejects the term occupation
nodes.what: A committee led by former Supreme Court justice Edmond Levy issued findings to the Netanyahu government concluding that Israel was not an occupying power in the West Bank and recommending legalization of many outposts. The report was welcomed by settler councils and rejected by Palestinian officials, the EU, and Israeli legal critics.
nodes.disputed: Settler councils and the Israeli right described the Levy report as restoring legal clarity; Palestinian negotiators and groups such as Yesh Din described it as a unilateral attempt to overturn the established international-law reading of the territory.

nodes.title: Knesset passes the Regularization Law
nodes.what: The Israeli parliament approved legislation retroactively legalizing thousands of settler homes built on privately owned Palestinian land, in exchange for compensation to the owners. The law was challenged in the High Court of Justice and struck down in June 2020.

nodes.title: US declares settlements not inconsistent with international law
nodes.what: Secretary of State Mike Pompeo announced that the United States no longer viewed Israeli civilian settlements in the West Bank as inherently inconsistent with international law, reversing a 1978 State Department legal opinion. The European Union and the Palestinian Authority rejected the shift.

nodes.title: Israeli cabinet authorizes nine outposts and new construction
nodes.what: The government led by Benjamin Netanyahu approved the legalization of nine previously unauthorized outposts in the West Bank and advanced planning for around 10,000 new settlement housing units. The decision drew condemnation from the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and Italy in a joint statement.

bands.label: Occupation and early settlement
bands.summary: Israeli military rule over the West Bank begins after the 1967 war and the first generation of civilian settlements and bypass roads is built before the Oslo framework.

nodes.title: Six-Day War ends with Israel in control of the West Bank
nodes.what: After six days of fighting with Egypt, Jordan, and Syria, Israeli forces took the West Bank and East Jerusalem from Jordanian control. A military government was established to administer the territory and its Palestinian population. The status of the territory under international law became the subject of immediate dispute.

nodes.title: UN Security Council passes Resolution 242
nodes.what: The Security Council adopted Resolution 242, calling for withdrawal of Israeli armed forces from territories occupied in the recent conflict and for a just and lasting peace in the Middle East. The wording of the withdrawal clause became a point of lasting disagreement between the parties.
nodes.disputed: Israeli officials describe the text as requiring withdrawal from some but not all territories taken in 1967; Arab states and many UN members describe it as requiring withdrawal from all territories occupied.

nodes.title: Kfar Etzion re-established as first West Bank settlement
nodes.what: A group of religious Israeli settlers received government approval to re-establish Kfar Etzion in the Etzion bloc south of Bethlehem. The site became the first Israeli civilian settlement in the West Bank after 1967 and a template for later settlement projects.

nodes.title: Israel passes the Jerusalem Law
nodes.what: The Knesset adopted a basic law declaring Jerusalem, complete and united, the capital of Israel, applying Israeli law to East Jerusalem and surrounding areas. The UN Security Council responded with Resolution 478 calling the law null and void and asking member states to withdraw diplomatic missions from the city.

nodes.title: First Intifada begins in the occupied territories
nodes.what: A Palestinian uprising broke out in Gaza and spread to the West Bank, marked by protests, strikes, stone-throwing, and clashes with Israeli forces. The uprising lasted into the early 1990s and reshaped Israeli policy debate and international attention on the occupation.
